SUPERSEDED.why: review of the link budget found two convention defects in the requirement derivation, and the fixed 2.96 uH matching value is not usable because the tuning inductance must be adjustable over 2.2-4.4 uH
what_still_stands: the 1.00 m vertical monopole antenna decision
the sideband check (recovered envelope 19999.9 Hz, duty 48.6%)
the detuning sensitivity warning (C +/-15% cuts current to about 1/3)
the rejection of three antenna models, including the failed MoM attempts
what_is_retracted: requirement of 5.30 mA rms: it is the result of h_eff = h/2 (inflates 2x) and an rms current divided by sqrt(2) (deflates 1.41x), net sqrt(2). The self-consistent value at D=3 is 3.75 mA rms

the driver margin '118%': it compares an ngspice rms current against a requirement already divided by sqrt(2). Apples-to-apples against its own model it is 83%. Against the corrected D-bracket (D=1.5 to 3) it is 112%-167%, which is the figure that should be quoted
the gap ratio 4.44x: it is 3.14x against the corrected D=3 requirement
the fixed L_match of 2.96 uH as a design value: C_ant from 6 to 12 pF requires 2.2-4.4 uH, so the coil must be adjustable
the implication that AM-ALT.3 is a closed stage: the antenna impedance is an unmeasured prerequisite, not a footnote, and blocks any v2 or 6 m conclusion
SUPERSEDED.does_not_change: the driver stage is still justified: every point of the corrected bracket (3.75-5.30 mA rms) exceeds the existing output ceiling of 1.19 mA rms by 3.1x-4.4x

question_answered: Which antenna, and what impedance does it present at 31 MHz?

antenna_decision.type: straight vertical monopole over the transmitter chassis/ground
antenna_decision.reason: course limit is 1 m; full length maximises R_rad and efficiency, and a monopole avoids balanced feed

impedance.confidence: engineering estimate from Schelkunoff's transmission-line approximation; NOT a full-wave solve and NOT a measurement
impedance.why: the capacitance depends on the ground plane, wire routing, nearby objects and hand proximity; a 15% error changes the antenna current by about 3x

rejected_models.why_rejected: collapses to ~0.10 of the correct radiation resistance at 0.103 lambda (verified in scripts/model_check.py); its early numbers 1.64 ohm / -189 ohm were wrong and are not used
rejected_models.kept_for: reproduces the half-wave and quarter-wave textbook references, so it is retained only as a validation fixture

rejected_models.why_rejected: three implementations failed the half-wave/quarter-wave checks (errors 20%-400%); deleted so no design number depends on an unvalidated solver
gives the wrong sign at 0.25 lambda (-350 ohm vs the true +21 ohm); used only as a lower bound on |X|

matching.topology: series L to resonate the antenna capacitance, antenna current sampled for tuning

sideband_check.verdict: 20 kHz AM sidebands pass the tuned antenna with no loss; the cost of the short antenna is efficiency, not bandwidth

interface_change.finding: the 1 kohm ROISO in the AM-ALT.2 output was sized for the 10k||5pF bench fixture and dissipates ~95% of the power into a 14 ohm antenna
interface_change.action: removed for the antenna interface; this is an AM-ALT.3 change and AM-ALT.2 files were not edited

driver.topology: common-emitter gain stage + emitter follower, two 2N3904

sensitivity.implication: tuning is mandatory and must be judged by antenna current, not by waveform shape

v3_redefined: voltage at the antenna feed point after the matching network; tp3 remains an internal modulator observation point and is not a course acceptance point
open_items: antenna impedance not measured: 8.91 pF is an estimate and the design is sensitive to it
6 m wireless communication not verified, and cannot be verified by simulation (AM-ALT.4)
receiver v2 not verified; AM-ALT.2 delivers m=22.5-24.3% while S05 was designed at m=50%, so v2 is roughly halved at the same field strength and must be recomputed
battery-side power is a budget, not a measurement
driver stage not built, antenna not built, no measurement of the ground return
